text:
Zayne Parekh is 20, in his first full season, and the headlines have moved fast: Daily Faceoff wrote that he is blossoming into a star in Calgary, and The Win Column asked whether he is already a top defenseman. The answer is not yet, but the trajectory is real.

He has 2 goals and 7 assists in 23 games, 5 of them on the power play, where he runs Calgary's top unit. His ice time is up 1.9 minutes over his last ten games to 19.4 a night. He has 41 shots.

He also compares well with history. Of the defensemen taken 7th to 11th overall since 2005 who have played four-plus seasons, the median scored 0.25 points a game in their first full season. He is at 0.39. The closest comparisons include Mikhail Sergachev and Dougie Hamilton.

The five-on-five game is around even: Calgary gets 50% of the expected goals with him on, 4.6 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, on a small sample, had him as a setup man. Watch the even-strength points. They are what turn a power-play specialist into a top defenseman.
headline: A power-play breakout
